key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage in perovskite solar cells, identifying preferential degradation at the buried hole-transport-layer interface.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive optical screening can guide interface design, with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification reducing buried-interface damage and improving UV stability.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe degradation at different depths.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL, and ideality factor measurements under UV soaking.
Compare perovskite films and p-i-n devices with different ITO surface modifiers.
evidence_signal: Non-destructive measurements localized UV-induced degradation to the HTL interface, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests, and showed improved UV stability with interface modification.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative stability gains or depth resolution, and performance under broader operational stress conditions remains to be established.
paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
